paper_id: AdapTrack_ Constrained Decoding without Distorting LLM's Output Intent
title: AdapTrack: Constrained Decoding without Distorting LLM's Output Intent
motivation: Constrained decoding forces the model to produce code satisfying constraints but misaligned with intent, e.g., ranking probability flips from 0.20% to 57.70% for undesired tokens.
problem_framing: Goal: sample distribution P(s|c) ∝ P(s)c(s) for valid sequences, preserving ratio P(s)/P(s′) between any two valid complete sequences s, s′.
key_insight: When a top-ranked token becomes invalid, backtrack by adaptive rejection sampling proportional to invalidated probability mass, not full resampling.
method_signature: AdapTrack: maintain Q[x] estimate of P(c|x), sample N[x] from P_Q(·|x), backtrack via Bernoulli rejection when Q drops.
evaluation_criteria: Exact match at k (EM@k) on TFv1 synthetic and TFv1Real real-world datasets; KL divergence on DSL problems; general benchmarks HumanEval/MBPP.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: AdapTrack invokes LM 20-60% more than constrained decoding, and requires longer backtracking distance for TensorFlow v2 settings (4-8 vs 2).
evidence_for_taste: deviate from the model's original output intent
truly misaligned with its output intent
wasteful of time and computational resources
thinking_moves: 从实际API调用失败案例出发，观察概率分布异常而非简单性能指标下降
将问题重新 frame 为采样分布保持问题，而非法则满足问题
借鉴人类写代码时的回退行为，提出自适应回退机制
用概率比值 formalize '意图扭曲' 程度，而非二元判断
